pt.L: E agora mandem depressa e contem a Davi, dizendo: 'Não passe a noite esta noite nas planícies do deserto, mas atravesse sem falta, para que o rei e todo o povo que [está] com ele não sejam tragados.'"
pt.B: Agora mandem avisar Davi depressa: 'Não acampe esta noite nas planícies junto ao deserto. Atravesse o rio sem falta, ou o rei e todo o povo que está com ele serão exterminados.'"
pt.R: Agora mandem logo uma mensagem a Davi. Digam a ele: 'Não fique esta noite no campo aberto perto do deserto. Atravesse o rio agora mesmo, ou o senhor e todo o seu povo serão destruídos!'"

am.L: አሁንም ፈጥናችሁ ላኩና ለዳዊት እንዲህ ብላችሁ ንገሩት፦ “ዛሬ ሌሊት በምድረ በዳው ሜዳዎች አይደሩ፤ ንጉሡና ከእርሱ ጋር ያለው ሕዝብ ሁሉ እንዳይዋጡ ፈጽመው ይሻገሩ እንጂ።”»
am.B: አሁንም ፈጥናችሁ ለዳዊት መልእክት ላኩና እንዲህ በሉት፦ “ዛሬ ሌሊት በምድረ በዳው አጠገብ ባለው ሜዳ አይስፈሩ። ያለ ምንም ጥርጥር ይሻገሩ፤ አለዚያ ንጉሡና ከእርሱ ጋር ያለው ሕዝብ ሁሉ ይጠፋሉ።”»
am.R: አሁንም ፈጥናችሁ ለዳዊት መልእክት ላኩ። እንዲህ በሉት፦ “ዛሬ ሌሊት በምድረ በዳው አጠገብ ባለው ገላጣ ስፍራ አይቆዩ። አሁኑኑ ወንዙን ይሻገሩ፤ አለዚያ እርስዎና ሕዝብዎ ሁሉ ይጠፋሉ!”»

decisions.choice: the plains of the wilderness
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked for reading aloud is "the plains", the low open land by the Jordan. The consonants written in the text could also be read "the fords", the river crossings. The same difference occurs at 15:28. Either way David is camped by the Jordan on the wilderness side.

decisions.choice: be sure to cross over: the verb is doubled for urgency
decisions.reason: Hushai cannot be certain that Absalom will hold to his advice; Ahithophel's plan could still be taken up. So David must not stay on the near side of the Jordan for even one night.

decisions.choice: be swallowed up: be utterly destroyed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is impersonal, "lest it be swallowed up for the king". To be swallowed up means to be wiped out completely (Lamentations 2:2, 5).

decisions.choice: you and all your people
decisions.reason: Hushai's message speaks of "the king" in the third person, as courtiers did. Readable has it address David directly.

decisions.choice: Cross the river
decisions.reason: Readable names what David is to cross: the Jordan (verse 22).

decisions.choice: "passe [le fleuve]" (L); "Passe le fleuve" (B)
decisions.reason: French "passer" needs an object here where the Hebrew "cross over" does not; the Jordan is meant (verse 22), so French names "le fleuve", bracketed at Literal.

decisions.choice: mandem, contem (to the priests); Não passe, atravesse (to David); o rei (L, B), o senhor (R)
decisions.reason: Hushai speaks to the two priests with the plural "vocês"; the message to David is a subject's word to his king, in the third person "o rei" at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable with "o senhor", which addresses David directly while keeping the courtesy, as the English Readable says "you". Balanced says "o rio" with "Atravesse", as Portuguese needs an object; it is the Jordan of verse 22.

decisions.choice: Hushai's message to David is in the respectful forms ("አይደሩ", "ይሻገሩ"; Readable "እርስዎና ሕዝብዎ").
decisions.reason: The words are addressed to the king through his messengers; Jonathan and Ahimaaz speak to him in the same forms in verse 21.

source.text: וִיהוֹנָתָ֨ן וַאֲחִימַ֜עַץ עֹמְדִ֣ים בְּעֵין־רֹגֵ֗ל וְהָלְכָ֤ה הַשִּׁפְחָה֙ וְהִגִּ֣ידָה לָהֶ֔ם וְהֵם֙ יֵֽלְכ֔וּ וְהִגִּ֖ידוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֛וּ לְהֵרָא֖וֹת לָב֥וֹא הָעִֽירָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz [were] standing at En-rogel, and would go the maidservant and would tell them, and they would go and would tell King David; for not they were able to be seen to come into the city.

en.L: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz [were] staying at En-rogel, and the servant girl would go and tell them, and they would go and tell King David, for they could not be seen coming into the city.
en.B: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En-rogel. A servant girl would go and pass the news to them, and they would go and tell King David, because they could not risk being seen entering the city.
en.R: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En-rogel, a spring just outside Jerusalem. A servant girl would go and give them the news, and then they would go and tell King David. They could not go into the city, because someone might see them.

es.L: Y Jonatán y Ahimaas se quedaban junto a En-roguel, y la sierva iba y les informaba, y ellos iban e informaban al rey David, porque no podían ser vistos entrando en la ciudad.
es.B: Jonatán y Ahimaas esperaban en En-roguel. Una criada iba y les pasaba las noticias, y ellos iban a contárselas al rey David, porque no podían arriesgarse a que los vieran entrar en la ciudad.
es.R: Jonatán y Ahimaas esperaban en En-roguel, un manantial a las afueras de Jerusalén. Una criada iba a darles las noticias, y luego ellos iban a contárselas al rey David. No podían entrar en la ciudad, porque alguien podía verlos.

fr.L: Et Jonathan et Ahimaats se tenaient à Èn-Roguel, et la servante allait les informer, et eux allaient informer le roi David, car ils ne pouvaient pas se faire voir en entrant dans la ville.
fr.B: Jonathan et Ahimaats attendaient à Èn-Roguel. Une servante allait leur transmettre les nouvelles, et eux allaient informer le roi David, car ils ne pouvaient pas risquer d’être vus en entrant dans la ville.
fr.R: Jonathan et Ahimaats attendaient à Èn-Roguel, une source tout près de Jérusalem. Une servante allait leur donner les nouvelles, et ensuite ils allaient les dire au roi David. Ils ne pouvaient pas entrer dans la ville, parce que quelqu’un aurait pu les voir.

sw.L: Yonathani na Ahimaasi [walikuwa] wakikaa En-rogeli, na mjakazi angekwenda kuwaambia, nao wangekwenda kumwambia Mfalme Daudi, kwa maana hawakuweza kuonekana wakiingia mjini.
sw.B: Yonathani na Ahimaasi walikuwa wakingoja huko En-rogeli. Mjakazi mmoja angekwenda kuwapa habari, nao wangekwenda kumwambia Mfalme Daudi, kwa sababu hawangeweza kuthubutu kuonekana wakiingia mjini.
sw.R: Yonathani na Ahimaasi walikuwa wakingoja huko En-rogeli, chemchemi iliyo nje kidogo ya Yerusalemu. Mjakazi mmoja angekwenda kuwapa habari, kisha wao wangekwenda kumwambia Mfalme Daudi. Hawakuweza kuingia mjini, kwa sababu mtu angeweza kuwaona.

vi.L: Giô-na-than và A-hi-mát [đang] ở tại Ên-Rô-ghên; một tớ gái sẽ đi báo tin cho họ, rồi họ sẽ đi báo cho vua Đa-vít, vì họ không thể để ai thấy mình vào thành.
vi.B: Giô-na-than và A-hi-mát đang chờ tại Ên-Rô-ghên. Một tớ gái sẽ đi báo tin cho họ, rồi họ sẽ đi báo cho vua Đa-vít, vì họ không dám để ai thấy mình vào thành.
vi.R: Giô-na-than và A-hi-mát đang chờ tại Ên-Rô-ghên, một con suối ngay bên ngoài Giê-ru-sa-lem. Một tớ gái sẽ đi báo tin cho họ, rồi họ sẽ đi báo cho vua Đa-vít. Họ không thể vào thành, vì sợ có người nhìn thấy.

ko.L: 요나단과 아히마아스는 엔로겔에 머물러 있었는데, 여종 하나가 가서 그들에게 알리면, 그들이 가서 다윗 왕에게 알리곤 했다. 그들이 성으로 들어가는 것을 남에게 보일 수 없었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 요나단과 아히마아스는 엔로겔에서 기다리고 있었다. 여종 하나가 가서 소식을 전해 주면, 그들이 가서 다윗 왕에게 알리기로 했다. 그들이 성에 드나드는 모습을 들켜서는 안 되었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 요나단과 아히마아스는 예루살렘 성 바로 밖에 있는 샘인 엔로겔에서 기다리고 있었다. 여종 하나가 가서 그들에게 소식을 전하면, 그들이 가서 다윗 왕에게 알리기로 했다. 그들은 누가 볼까 봐 성 안으로 들어갈 수 없었다.

pt.L: E Jônatas e Aimaás [estavam] parados em En-Rogel, e a serva ia e lhes contava, e eles iam e contavam ao rei Davi; pois não podiam ser vistos entrando na cidade.
pt.B: Jônatas e Aimaás estavam esperando em En-Rogel. Uma serva ia lhes passar as notícias, e eles iam contá-las ao rei Davi, porque não podiam arriscar ser vistos entrando na cidade.
pt.R: Jônatas e Aimaás estavam esperando em En-Rogel, uma fonte logo fora de Jerusalém. Uma serva ia levar as notícias a eles, e depois eles iam contar tudo ao rei Davi. Eles não podiam entrar na cidade, porque alguém poderia vê-los.

am.L: ዮናታንና አኪማአስም በዓይንሮጌል ይቆሙ ነበር፤ አንዲት ሴት አገልጋይም ሄዳ ትነግራቸው ነበር፤ እነርሱም ሄደው ለንጉሡ ለዳዊት ይነግሩት ነበር፤ ወደ ከተማዪቱ ሲገቡ ሊታዩ አይችሉም ነበርና።
am.B: ዮናታንና አኪማአስ በዓይንሮጌል ይጠባበቁ ነበር። አንዲት ሴት አገልጋይ ሄዳ ወሬውን ታደርስላቸው ነበር፤ እነርሱም ሄደው ለንጉሡ ለዳዊት ይነግሩት ነበር፤ ወደ ከተማዪቱ ሲገቡ መታየት አልነበረባቸውም።
am.R: ዮናታንና አኪማአስ ከኢየሩሳሌም ወጣ ብሎ ባለው በዓይንሮጌል ምንጭ ይጠባበቁ ነበር። አንዲት ሴት አገልጋይ ሄዳ ወሬውን ትነግራቸው ነበር፤ ከዚያም እነርሱ ሄደው ለንጉሡ ለዳዊት ይነግሩት ነበር። አንድ ሰው ሊያያቸው ስለሚችል ወደ ከተማዪቱ መግባት አይችሉም ነበር።

decisions.choice: Jonathan and Ahimaaz: the sons of the two priests
decisions.reason: Jonathan was Abiathar's son and Ahimaaz was Zadok's son. David had named them as the messengers who would bring him news (15:27, 36).

decisions.choice: En-rogel: a spring just outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: En-rogel was a spring in the valley south-east of the city, on the border between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:7; 18:16; 1 Kings 1:9).

decisions.choice: would go ... would tell: the arrangement the messengers worked by
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe a plan set up in advance, or a practice repeated, rather than one event. A servant girl going out of the city, perhaps to fetch water at the spring, would draw no attention.

decisions.choice: servant girl: a female servant
decisions.reason: The word names a woman servant of a household. The text does not say whose household she belonged to.

decisions.choice: a spring just outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable explains what En-rogel was and so why the young men could wait there.

decisions.choice: Èn-Roguel
decisions.reason: The French transcription of the name ("Source of the fuller"), with "gu" to keep the hard g; kept for both books.

decisions.choice: En-roguel
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish spelling of the spring's name, with 'gu' so that it is read with a hard g.

decisions.choice: "Ên-Rô-ghên"
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese form, kept through Samuel.

decisions.choice: Jônatas; Aimaás; En-Rogel; a serva
decisions.reason: "Jônatas" (Abiathar's son, m1) has the same form as Saul's son in 1 Samuel, as in 15:27, 36; "Aimaás" as the chapters before; "En-Rogel" as Joshua 15:7 in Portuguese (m2). "Serva" is the plain word for a woman servant of a household (m4).

source.text: וַיַּ֤רְא אֹתָם֙ נַ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ שְׁנֵיהֶ֨ם מְהֵרָ֜ה וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ׀אֶל־בֵּֽית־אִ֣ישׁ בְּבַחוּרִ֗ים וְל֥וֹ בְאֵ֛ר בַּחֲצֵר֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥רְדוּ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw them a young man and told Absalom; and went the two of them quickly and came to [the] house of a man in Bahurim, and to him [was] a well in his courtyard, and they went down there.

en.L: But a young man saw them and told Absalom. And the two of them went quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, and he [had] a well in his courtyard, and they went down there.
en.B: But a young man spotted them and told Absalom. So the two hurried off to Bahurim, to the house of a man whose courtyard had a well, and they climbed down into it.
en.R: But a young man saw them and reported it to Absalom. So the two of them hurried away to the village of Bahurim. A man there had a well in his courtyard, and the two young men let themselves down into it to hide.

es.L: Pero los vio un joven y se lo dijo a Absalón. Y los dos se fueron de prisa y llegaron a la casa de un hombre en Bahurim, que tenía un pozo en su patio, y bajaron allí.
es.B: Pero un joven los vio y se lo contó a Absalón. Así que los dos se fueron de prisa a Bahurim, a la casa de un hombre que tenía un pozo en el patio, y se metieron en él.
es.R: Pero un joven los vio y se lo contó a Absalón. Así que los dos se fueron de prisa al pueblo de Bahurim. Allí un hombre tenía un pozo en su patio, y los dos jóvenes se metieron en él para esconderse.

fr.L: Mais un jeune homme les vit et informa Absalom. Et tous deux s’en allèrent vite et arrivèrent à la maison d’un homme à Bahourim, et il [avait] un puits dans sa cour, et ils y descendirent.
fr.B: Mais un jeune homme les aperçut et prévint Absalom. Les deux partirent donc en hâte et arrivèrent à Bahourim, chez un homme qui avait un puits dans sa cour ; ils y descendirent.
fr.R: Mais un jeune homme les a vus et l’a dit à Absalom. Les deux jeunes gens sont donc partis très vite jusqu’au village de Bahourim. Là, un homme avait un puits dans sa cour, et ils sont descendus dedans pour se cacher.

sw.L: Lakini kijana mmoja akawaona akamwambia Absalomu. Wao wawili wakaenda upesi, wakafika nyumbani kwa mtu mmoja huko Bahurimu, naye [alikuwa na] kisima uani mwake, nao wakashuka humo.
sw.B: Lakini kijana mmoja akawaona, akamwambia Absalomu. Basi wale wawili wakaondoka upesi, wakaenda Bahurimu nyumbani kwa mtu mmoja aliyekuwa na kisima uani mwake, nao wakashuka ndani yake.
sw.R: Lakini kijana mmoja akawaona, akamwarifu Absalomu. Basi wale wawili wakaondoka haraka, wakaenda kijiji cha Bahurimu. Mtu mmoja huko alikuwa na kisima uani mwake, na wale vijana wawili wakashuka ndani yake ili kujificha.

vi.L: Nhưng có một thanh niên thấy họ và báo cho Áp-sa-lôm. Hai người vội vã đi đến nhà một người ở Ba-hu-rim; trong sân nhà người ấy có một cái giếng, và họ xuống đó.
vi.B: Nhưng một thanh niên trông thấy họ và báo cho Áp-sa-lôm. Vậy hai người vội vàng đến Ba-hu-rim, vào nhà một người có cái giếng trong sân, và họ leo xuống giếng.
vi.R: Nhưng một thanh niên trông thấy họ và báo cho Áp-sa-lôm. Vậy hai người vội vàng đến làng Ba-hu-rim. Ở đó có một người có cái giếng trong sân, và hai chàng trai leo xuống giếng để trốn.

ko.L: 그러나 한 젊은이가 그들을 보고 압살롬에게 알렸다. 그래서 그 두 사람은 급히 가서 바후림에 있는 어떤 사람의 집에 이르렀는데, 그의 뜰에 우물이 있어서 그들이 그리로 내려갔다.
ko.B: 그러나 한 젊은이가 그들을 보고 압살롬에게 알렸다. 그래서 두 사람은 서둘러 바후림으로 가서, 뜰에 우물이 있는 어떤 사람의 집에 이르렀다. 그들은 그 우물 속으로 내려갔다.
ko.R: 그런데 한 젊은이가 그들을 보고 압살롬에게 알렸다. 그래서 두 사람은 서둘러 바후림 마을로 갔다. 그곳에 사는 한 사람의 집 뜰에 우물이 있었다. 두 사람은 숨으려고 그 우물 속으로 내려갔다.

pt.L: Mas um moço os viu e contou a Absalão. E os dois foram depressa e chegaram à casa de um homem em Baurim, e ele [tinha] um poço no seu pátio, e desceram ali.
pt.B: Mas um rapaz os viu e avisou Absalão. Então os dois saíram depressa e chegaram a Baurim, à casa de um homem que tinha um poço no pátio, e desceram para dentro dele.
pt.R: Mas um rapaz viu os dois e contou a Absalão. Então eles saíram correndo para o povoado de Baurim. Um homem dali tinha um poço no pátio da casa, e os dois desceram até lá dentro para se esconder.

am.L: ነገር ግን አንድ ወጣት አያቸውና ለአቤሴሎም ነገረው፤ ሁለቱም ፈጥነው ሄዱ፤ በባሑሪምም ወዳለ ወደ አንድ ሰው ቤት መጡ፤ በግቢውም ውስጥ የውኃ ጉድጓድ ነበረው፤ ወደዚያም ወረዱ።
am.B: ነገር ግን አንድ ወጣት አያቸውና ለአቤሴሎም ነገረው። ስለዚህ ሁለቱ ፈጥነው ወደ ባሑሪም ሄዱ፤ በግቢው ውስጥ የውኃ ጉድጓድ ወዳለው ወደ አንድ ሰው ቤት ደርሰው ወደ ጉድጓዱ ወረዱ።
am.R: ነገር ግን አንድ ወጣት አያቸውና ለአቤሴሎም ነገረው። ስለዚህ ሁለቱ ፈጥነው ወደ ባሑሪም መንደር ሄዱ። በዚያ የሚኖር አንድ ሰው በግቢው ውስጥ የውኃ ጉድጓድ ነበረው፤ ሁለቱ ወጣቶች ለመደበቅ ወደ ጉድጓዱ ወረዱ።

decisions.choice: Bahurim: a village on the road from Jerusalem to the Jordan
decisions.reason: Bahurim lay just east of the Mount of Olives. It was Shimei's home, where he cursed David (16:5); here a household in the same village helps David's men.

decisions.choice: well: a shaft dug in the ground, here probably dry
decisions.reason: The word normally names a well dug down to water. Since two men could hide in this one, it was probably dry or nearly so, perhaps a cistern for storing rainwater.

decisions.choice: a young man: a boy or a servant
decisions.reason: The word can mean a youth or a young servant. Who he was, the text does not say; he was on Absalom's side.

decisions.choice: climbed down into it
decisions.reason: "Went down there" means into the well itself, as verse 21 shows.

decisions.choice: to hide
decisions.reason: Readable says why they went down into the well.

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וַתִּפְרֹ֤שׂ אֶת־הַמָּסָךְ֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַתִּשְׁטַ֥ח עָלָ֖יו הָֽרִפ֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And took the woman and spread the covering over [the] face of the well, and spread on it the groats, and not was known a thing.

en.L: And the woman took the covering and spread [it] over the face of the well, and scattered the groats on it, and nothing was known.
en.B: The woman of the house took a covering, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered grain on it, so that nothing could be seen.
en.R: The woman of the house took a cover and spread it over the opening of the well. Then she scattered grain on top of it, so no one could tell that anything was there.

es.L: Y la mujer tomó la cubierta y [la] extendió sobre la boca del pozo, y esparció sobre ella el grano trillado, y no se supo nada.
es.B: La mujer de la casa tomó una manta, la extendió sobre la boca del pozo y esparció grano encima, de modo que no se notaba nada.
es.R: La mujer de la casa tomó una manta y la extendió sobre la boca del pozo. Luego esparció grano encima, para que nadie pudiera darse cuenta de que había algo allí.

fr.L: Et la femme prit la couverture, et l’étendit sur l’ouverture du puits, et y répandit du grain broyé, et on ne sut rien.
fr.B: La femme de la maison prit une couverture, l’étendit sur l’ouverture du puits et y répandit du grain, si bien qu’on ne remarquait rien.
fr.R: La femme de la maison a pris une couverture et l’a étendue sur l’ouverture du puits. Puis elle a répandu du grain dessus. Comme ça, personne ne pouvait savoir qu’il y avait quelque chose là.

sw.L: Mwanamke akachukua kifuniko akakitandaza juu ya uso wa kisima, akanyunyiza nafaka iliyopondwa juu yake, wala hakuna kilichojulikana.
sw.B: Mwanamke wa nyumba ile akachukua kifuniko, akakitandaza juu ya mdomo wa kisima, akaanika nafaka juu yake, hata hakuna kilichoweza kuonekana.
sw.R: Mwanamke wa nyumba ile akachukua kifuniko, akakitandaza juu ya mdomo wa kisima. Kisha akaanika nafaka juu yake, hata hakuna mtu aliyeweza kujua kwamba kuna kitu humo.

vi.L: Người đàn bà lấy tấm che trải lên miệng giếng, rồi rải lúa xay lên trên, và không ai biết gì cả.
vi.B: Bà chủ nhà lấy một tấm che trải lên miệng giếng rồi rải lúa lên trên, nên không ai nhận ra được.
vi.R: Bà chủ nhà lấy một tấm che đậy lên miệng giếng. Rồi bà rải lúa lên trên, nên không ai biết có gì ở đó.

ko.L: 그 여자가 덮개를 가져다가 우물 아귀에 펴고, 그 위에 찧은 곡식을 널어 놓으니, 아무것도 알려지지 않았다.
ko.B: 그 집 여자는 덮개를 가져다가 우물 입구에 펴고, 그 위에 곡식을 널어 놓았다. 그래서 아무것도 눈에 띄지 않았다.
ko.R: 그 집 여자는 덮개를 가져와 우물 입구를 덮었다. 그리고 그 위에 곡식을 널어 놓았다. 그래서 아무도 그 아래에 무엇이 있는지 알 수 없었다.

pt.L: E a mulher tomou a coberta e [a] estendeu sobre a boca do poço, e espalhou sobre ela grão pilado, e nada se soube.
pt.B: A mulher da casa pegou uma coberta, estendeu-a sobre a boca do poço e espalhou grãos em cima, de modo que nada se percebia.
pt.R: A mulher da casa pegou uma coberta e a estendeu sobre a abertura do poço. Depois espalhou grãos por cima, para que ninguém percebesse que havia alguma coisa ali.

am.L: ሴቲቱም መሸፈኛውን ወስዳ በጉድጓዱ አፍ ላይ ዘረጋችው፤ በላዩም የተከካ እህል በተነች፤ ምንም ነገርም አልታወቀም።
am.B: የቤቱ እመቤትም መሸፈኛ ወስዳ በጉድጓዱ አፍ ላይ ዘረጋች፤ በላዩም እህል በተነች፤ ስለዚህ ምንም ነገር አልታየም።
am.R: የቤቱ እመቤትም መሸፈኛ ወስዳ በጉድጓዱ አፍ ላይ ዘረጋች። ከዚያም በላዩ ላይ እህል በተነች፤ ስለዚህ በዚያ ምንም ነገር እንዳለ ማንም ሊያውቅ አልቻለም።

decisions.choice: groats: crushed or husked grain
decisions.reason: The word is rare (elsewhere only Proverbs 27:22) and seems to mean grain that has been crushed or pounded. Grain spread out to dry in a courtyard was an everyday sight.

decisions.choice: the covering: a cloth or screen
decisions.reason: The noun names something spread to cover or screen, the same word used of the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:36).

decisions.choice: the woman: the wife of the house
decisions.reason: "The woman" is the woman of the house where the men hid, most likely the householder's wife. Like Rahab with the spies (Joshua 2:4-6), she hides the messengers.

decisions.choice: The woman of the house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which woman is meant.

decisions.choice: nothing could be seen; no one could tell that anything was there
decisions.reason: "Nothing was known" means the hiding place could not be detected.

decisions.choice: grão pilado
decisions.reason: Literal names grain that has been crushed or pounded (m1) without guessing which grain; Balanced and Readable say "grãos", as the English says "grain".

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַבְדֵי֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֶֽל־הָאִשָּׁ֜ה הַבַּ֗יְתָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַיֵּ֗ה אֲחִימַ֨עַץ֙ וִיה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה עָבְר֖וּ מִיכַ֣ל הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֔אוּ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] servants of Absalom to the woman to the house and said, where [are] Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And said to them the woman, they have crossed [the] stream of the water. And they searched and not found, and they returned [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house and said, "Where [are] Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They have crossed the stream of water." And they searched and did not find [them], and they returned [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: Absalom's servants came to the house and asked the woman, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman told them, "They have gone across the stream." They searched but could not find them, so they went back to Jerusalem.
en.R: Absalom's servants came to the house and asked the woman, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" She answered, "They went across the stream." The men looked for them but could not find them, so they went back to Jerusalem.

es.L: Y los siervos de Absalón vinieron a la mujer a la casa y dijeron: «¿Dónde [están] Ahimaas y Jonatán?». Y la mujer les dijo: «Han pasado el arroyo de agua». Y buscaron y no [los] hallaron, y volvieron [a] Jerusalén.
es.B: Los siervos de Absalón llegaron a la casa y le preguntaron a la mujer: «¿Dónde están Ahimaas y Jonatán?». La mujer les dijo: «Se fueron al otro lado del arroyo». Los buscaron, pero no los encontraron, así que volvieron a Jerusalén.
es.R: Los siervos de Absalón llegaron a la casa y le preguntaron a la mujer: «¿Dónde están Ahimaas y Jonatán?». Ella respondió: «Cruzaron el arroyo». Los hombres los buscaron, pero no los encontraron, así que regresaron a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et les serviteurs d’Absalom vinrent vers la femme, à la maison, et dirent : « Où [sont] Ahimaats et Jonathan ? » Et la femme leur dit : « Ils ont passé le ruisseau d’eau. » Et ils cherchèrent et ne [les] trouvèrent pas, et ils retournèrent [à] Jérusalem.
fr.B: Les serviteurs d’Absalom arrivèrent à la maison et demandèrent à la femme : « Où sont Ahimaats et Jonathan ? » La femme leur répondit : « Ils ont traversé le ruisseau. » Ils cherchèrent, mais ne les trouvèrent pas, et ils retournèrent à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Les serviteurs d’Absalom sont arrivés à la maison et ont demandé à la femme : « Où sont Ahimaats et Jonathan ? » Elle a répondu : « Ils ont traversé le ruisseau. » Les hommes les ont cherchés, mais ils ne les ont pas trouvés. Alors ils sont retournés à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Watumishi wa Absalomu wakaja kwa yule mwanamke nyumbani, wakasema, "Ahimaasi na Yonathani [wako] wapi?" Yule mwanamke akawaambia, "Wamevuka kijito cha maji." Wakatafuta wasiwapate, wakarudi Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Watumishi wa Absalomu walipofika nyumbani wakamwuliza yule mwanamke, "Ahimaasi na Yonathani wako wapi?" Yule mwanamke akawaambia, "Wamevuka kijito." Wakawatafuta lakini hawakuwapata, basi wakarudi Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Watumishi wa Absalomu wakafika nyumbani wakamwuliza yule mwanamke, "Ahimaasi na Yonathani wako wapi?" Akajibu, "Wamevuka kijito." Wale watu wakawatafuta lakini hawakuwapata, basi wakarudi Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Các đầy tớ của Áp-sa-lôm đến nhà người đàn bà và hỏi: "A-hi-mát và Giô-na-than [ở] đâu?" Người đàn bà nói với họ: "Họ đã qua dòng nước rồi." Họ tìm mà không thấy, nên trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Các đầy tớ của Áp-sa-lôm đến nhà ấy và hỏi người đàn bà: "A-hi-mát và Giô-na-than đâu?" Bà đáp: "Họ đã qua suối rồi." Họ tìm kiếm mà không thấy, nên quay về Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Các đầy tớ của Áp-sa-lôm đến nhà ấy và hỏi người đàn bà: "A-hi-mát và Giô-na-than đâu?" Bà trả lời: "Họ đã qua suối rồi." Họ đi tìm nhưng không thấy, nên quay về Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 압살롬의 종들이 그 집의 여자에게 와서 말했다. "아히마아스와 요나단이 어디 있느냐?" 그 여자가 그들에게 말했다. "그들은 시냇물을 건너갔습니다." 그들이 찾아보았으나 찾지 못하고 예루살렘으로 돌아갔다.
ko.B: 압살롬의 종들이 그 집에 와서 여자에게 물었다. "아히마아스와 요나단은 어디 있느냐?" 여자가 그들에게 대답했다. "그들은 시내를 건너갔습니다." 그들은 찾아보았으나 찾지 못하자 예루살렘으로 돌아갔다.
ko.R: 압살롬의 종들이 그 집에 와서 여자에게 물었다. "아히마아스와 요나단은 어디 있느냐?" 여자가 대답했다. "시내를 건너갔습니다." 그들은 두 사람을 찾아다녔지만 찾지 못하고 예루살렘으로 돌아갔다.

pt.L: E os servos de Absalão vieram à mulher, à casa, e disseram: "Onde [estão] Aimaás e Jônatas?" E a mulher lhes disse: "Passaram o riacho das águas." E procuraram e não [os] acharam, e voltaram [a] Jerusalém.
pt.B: Os servos de Absalão chegaram à casa e perguntaram à mulher: "Onde estão Aimaás e Jônatas?" A mulher lhes respondeu: "Atravessaram o riacho." Eles procuraram, mas não os acharam, e voltaram para Jerusalém.
pt.R: Os servos de Absalão chegaram à casa e perguntaram à mulher: "Onde estão Aimaás e Jônatas?" Ela respondeu: "Atravessaram o riacho." Os homens procuraram os dois, mas não os encontraram. Por isso voltaram para Jerusalém.

am.L: የአቤሴሎምም ባሪያዎች ወደ ሴቲቱ ወደ ቤቱ መጥተው፦ «አኪማአስና ዮናታን ወዴት [ናቸው]?» አሉ። ሴቲቱም፦ «የውኃውን ጅረት ተሻግረዋል» አለቻቸው። ፈለጉ፤ አላገኙምም፤ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምም ተመለሱ።
am.B: የአቤሴሎም አገልጋዮች ወደ ቤቱ መጥተው ሴቲቱን፦ «አኪማአስና ዮናታን የት ናቸው?» ብለው ጠየቋት። ሴቲቱም፦ «ጅረቱን ተሻግረው ሄደዋል» አለቻቸው። ፈለጓቸው፤ ግን ሊያገኟቸው አልቻሉም፤ ስለዚህ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሱ።
am.R: የአቤሴሎም አገልጋዮች ወደ ቤቱ መጥተው ሴቲቱን፦ «አኪማአስና ዮናታን የት ናቸው?» ብለው ጠየቋት። እርሷም፦ «ጅረቱን ተሻግረው ሄዱ» ብላ መለሰች። ሰዎቹ ፈለጓቸው፤ ግን ሊያገኟቸው አልቻሉም፤ ስለዚህ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሱ።

decisions.choice: the stream of water: meaning uncertain
decisions.reason: The first word occurs only here. It may mean a small stream or channel of water, perhaps a brook near Bahurim. Some take it as the edge of the water, the Jordan itself; others think it is a place name. The woman's point is clear: the men have gone on beyond reach.

decisions.choice: the woman sends the searchers away: like Rahab
decisions.reason: Like Rahab, who hid the spies on her roof and sent the king's men off in the wrong direction (Joshua 2:4-7), and like Michal, who misled Saul's men to save David (1 Samuel 19:12-17), this woman protects David's messengers by misleading his enemies. The text tells what she did without comment.

decisions.choice: Absalom's servants: men sent by the new king
decisions.reason: The servants of a king are his officials and agents; here they are the men Absalom sent to catch the messengers.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep "servants" here: these are not court officials but men carrying out Absalom's orders.

decisions.choice: o riacho das águas (L); o riacho (B, R)
decisions.reason: The rare word is uncertain (m1); "riacho" says a small stream, the reading the English follows, without naming the Jordan.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀אַחֲרֵ֣י לֶכְתָּ֗ם וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ מֵֽהַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד ק֣וּמוּ וְעִבְר֤וּ מְהֵרָה֙ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם כִּי־כָ֛כָה יָעַ֥ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֲחִיתֹֽפֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after their going, and they came up from the well and went and told King David, and said to David, arise and cross quickly the water, for thus has counseled against you Ahithophel.

en.L: And it was after they had gone, that they came up from the well and went and told King David, and they said to David, "Arise and cross the water quickly, for thus Ahithophel has counseled against you."
en.B: After the men had left, the two climbed out of the well and went to tell King David. They said to David, "Get up and cross the water at once, for this is what Ahithophel has advised against you."
en.R: After Absalom's men left, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well and went to report to King David. They told him, "Hurry and get across the river now! Ahithophel has given advice to attack you."

es.L: Y sucedió, después que se fueron, que subieron del pozo y fueron e informaron al rey David, y dijeron a David: «Levántate y pasa de prisa el agua, porque así ha aconsejado Ahitofel contra ti».
es.B: Cuando los hombres se fueron, los dos salieron del pozo y fueron a avisar al rey David. Le dijeron: «Levántate y cruza el agua enseguida, porque esto es lo que Ahitofel ha aconsejado contra ti».
es.R: Después que se fueron los hombres de Absalón, Jonatán y Ahimaas salieron del pozo y fueron a informar al rey David. Le dijeron: «¡Date prisa y cruza ahora mismo el río! Ahitofel ha aconsejado que te ataquen».

fr.L: Et après leur départ, ils remontèrent du puits, et allèrent informer le roi David, et dirent à David : « Levez-vous et passez vite l’eau, car voici ce qu’Ahitofel a conseillé contre vous. »
fr.B: Quand les hommes furent partis, les deux jeunes gens remontèrent du puits et allèrent informer le roi David. Ils dirent à David : « Levez-vous et traversez l’eau tout de suite, car voici ce qu’Ahitofel a conseillé contre vous. »
fr.R: Quand les hommes d’Absalom sont partis, Jonathan et Ahimaats sont sortis du puits et sont allés tout raconter au roi David. Ils lui ont dit : « Vite, traversez le fleuve maintenant ! Ahitofel a conseillé de vous attaquer. »

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya kuondoka kwao, wakapanda kutoka kisimani, wakaenda wakamwambia Mfalme Daudi, wakamwambia Daudi, "Inuka uvuke maji upesi, kwa maana hivi ndivyo Ahithofeli alivyoshauri juu yako."
sw.B: Watu wale walipokwisha kuondoka, wale wawili wakapanda kutoka kisimani, wakaenda kumwambia Mfalme Daudi. Wakamwambia Daudi, "Inuka uvuke maji mara moja, kwa maana hivi ndivyo Ahithofeli alivyoshauri dhidi yako."
sw.R: Watu wa Absalomu walipokwisha kuondoka, Yonathani na Ahimaasi wakapanda kutoka kisimani, wakaenda kumpa Mfalme Daudi habari. Wakamwambia, "Fanya haraka uvuke mto sasa hivi! Ahithofeli ametoa ushauri wa kukushambulia."

vi.L: Sau khi họ đi rồi, hai người từ giếng leo lên, đi báo cho vua Đa-vít. Họ nói với Đa-vít: "Xin vua hãy đứng dậy mau qua sông, vì A-hi-tô-phe đã bày mưu như thế này để hại vua."
vi.B: Khi bọn ấy đi rồi, hai người leo lên khỏi giếng và đi báo cho vua Đa-vít. Họ thưa với Đa-vít: "Xin bệ hạ đứng dậy qua sông ngay, vì A-hi-tô-phe đã bày mưu như thế để hại bệ hạ."
vi.R: Sau khi người của Áp-sa-lôm đi rồi, Giô-na-than và A-hi-mát leo lên khỏi giếng và đi báo cho vua Đa-vít. Họ thưa: "Xin đức vua mau qua sông ngay bây giờ! A-hi-tô-phe đã khuyên tấn công đức vua."

ko.L: 그들이 간 뒤에 두 사람이 우물에서 올라와 가서 다윗 왕에게 알렸다. 그들이 다윗에게 말했다. "일어나 빨리 물을 건너십시오. 아히도벨이 임금님을 치려고 이렇게 계책을 냈습니다."
ko.B: 그 사람들이 떠난 뒤에 두 사람은 우물에서 올라와 다윗 왕에게 가서 알렸다. 그들이 다윗에게 말했다. "일어나서 어서 물을 건너십시오. 아히도벨이 임금님을 치려고 이런 계책을 냈습니다."
ko.R: 압살롬의 부하들이 떠난 뒤에 요나단과 아히마아스는 우물에서 올라와 다윗 왕에게 가서 알렸다. 그들이 말했다. "서둘러 지금 강을 건너십시오! 아히도벨이 임금님을 치라는 계책을 냈습니다."

pt.L: E aconteceu, depois que eles se foram, que subiram do poço e foram e contaram ao rei Davi, e disseram a Davi: "Levantem-se e atravessem depressa a água, porque assim Aitofel aconselhou contra vocês."
pt.B: Depois que os homens se foram, os dois saíram do poço e foram contar ao rei Davi. Disseram a Davi: "Levantem-se e atravessem a água agora mesmo, porque foi isto o que Aitofel aconselhou contra vocês."
pt.R: Depois que os homens de Absalão foram embora, Jônatas e Aimaás saíram do poço e foram contar tudo ao rei Davi. Disseram a ele: "Depressa! Atravessem o rio agora! Aitofel deu um conselho para atacar vocês."

am.L: ከሄዱም በኋላ እንዲህ ሆነ፤ ከጉድጓዱ ወጥተው ሄዱ፤ ለንጉሡ ለዳዊትም ነገሩት፤ ዳዊትንም፦ «አኪጦፌል በእርስዎ ላይ እንዲህ መክሯልና ተነሡ፤ ውኃውንም ፈጥነው ይሻገሩ» አሉት።
am.B: ሰዎቹ ከሄዱ በኋላ ሁለቱ ከጉድጓዱ ወጥተው ለንጉሡ ለዳዊት ሊነግሩት ሄዱ። ዳዊትንም፦ «አኪጦፌል በእርስዎ ላይ እንዲህ መክሯልና ተነሡ፤ ውኃውን አሁኑኑ ይሻገሩ» አሉት።
am.R: የአቤሴሎም ሰዎች ከሄዱ በኋላ ዮናታንና አኪማአስ ከጉድጓዱ ወጥተው ለንጉሡ ለዳዊት ሊነግሩት ሄዱ። እንዲህም አሉት፦ «ፈጥነው አሁኑኑ ወንዙን ይሻገሩ! አኪጦፌል በእርስዎ ላይ አደጋ እንዲጣል መክሯል።»

decisions.choice: thus Ahithophel has counseled against you: they report the danger, Ahithophel's plan
decisions.reason: The messengers speak of Ahithophel's plan for a quick night attack, not of Hushai's, because that was the danger to be escaped: Absalom might yet change his mind (verse 16). "Against you" is plural, meaning David and the people with him.

decisions.choice: the water: the Jordan
decisions.reason: "The water" is the river Jordan, which David's company crosses in the next verse.

decisions.choice: Absalom's men; Jonathan and Ahimaaz
decisions.reason: Readable names who left and who came up, since the Hebrew uses only "they" for both groups.

decisions.choice: the river
decisions.reason: Readable says "river" so that the reader knows which water is meant (see m2).

decisions.choice: "vous" (plural) for "arise and cross" and "against you"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew commands are plural: the messengers speak to David and the people with him, who all cross in verse 22. French makes this plain with "vous".

decisions.choice: Levantem-se, atravessem; contra vocês (plural)
decisions.reason: The commands and "against you" are plural in Hebrew (m1), meant for David and all his company, so Portuguese uses the plural "vocês", which it can show and English cannot; addressed to the whole company, it carries no slight to the king.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וְכָל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן עַד־א֣וֹר הַבֹּ֗קֶר עַד־אַחַד֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־עָבַ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose David and all the people who [were] with him, and they crossed the Jordan; until [the] light of the morning, until one not was missing who not had crossed the Jordan.

en.L: And David arose, and all the people who [were] with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By the light of the morning not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.
en.B: So David and all the people with him set out and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak not a single one was left who had not crossed the Jordan.
en.R: So David and all his people got up and crossed the Jordan River. By sunrise every one of them was across.

es.L: Y David se levantó, y todo el pueblo que [estaba] con él, y pasaron el Jordán. Para la luz de la mañana no faltaba ni uno que no hubiera pasado el Jordán.
es.B: Así que David y toda la gente que estaba con él se pusieron en marcha y cruzaron el Jordán. Al amanecer no quedaba ni uno solo que no hubiera cruzado el Jordán.
es.R: Así que David y toda su gente se levantaron y cruzaron el río Jordán. Al salir el sol, todos ya estaban al otro lado.

fr.L: Et David se leva, et tout le peuple qui [était] avec lui, et ils passèrent le Jourdain. À la lumière du matin, il n’en manquait pas un seul qui n’eût passé le Jourdain.
fr.B: David et tout le peuple qui l’accompagnait partirent donc et passèrent le Jourdain. Au lever du jour, il n’en restait pas un seul qui n’eût traversé le Jourdain.
fr.R: David et tout son peuple se sont donc levés et ont traversé le Jourdain. Au lever du soleil, ils étaient tous de l’autre côté.

sw.L: Daudi akainuka, na watu wote [waliokuwa] pamoja naye, wakavuka Yordani. Kufikia mwanga wa asubuhi hakukosekana hata mmoja ambaye hakuwa amevuka Yordani.
sw.B: Basi Daudi na watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye wakaondoka, wakavuka Yordani. Kufikia mapambazuko hakubaki hata mmoja ambaye hakuwa amevuka Yordani.
sw.R: Basi Daudi na watu wake wote wakaondoka, wakavuka mto Yordani. Jua lilipochomoza, kila mmoja wao alikuwa amevuka.

vi.L: Đa-vít và toàn dân theo vua đứng dậy và qua sông Giô-đanh. Đến lúc trời sáng, không thiếu một người nào chưa qua sông Giô-đanh.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít và toàn dân theo vua lên đường qua sông Giô-đanh. Đến rạng sáng, không còn một người nào chưa qua sông Giô-đanh.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít và tất cả người của vua đứng dậy qua sông Giô-đanh. Đến lúc mặt trời mọc, mọi người đều đã sang bên kia sông.

ko.L: 다윗과 그와 함께 있는 모든 백성이 일어나 요단강을 건넜다. 아침 햇빛이 비칠 무렵에는 요단강을 건너지 않고 남은 사람이 하나도 없었다.
ko.B: 그래서 다윗과 그와 함께 있는 모든 백성은 일어나 요단강을 건넜다. 동틀 무렵에는 요단강을 건너지 않은 사람이 하나도 없었다.
ko.R: 그래서 다윗과 그의 백성은 모두 일어나 요단강을 건넜다. 해가 뜰 무렵에는 모두 강을 다 건넜다.

pt.L: E Davi se levantou, e todo o povo que [estava] com ele, e atravessaram o Jordão. Até a luz da manhã, não faltou nem um que não tivesse atravessado o Jordão.
pt.B: Então Davi e todo o povo que estava com ele partiram e atravessaram o Jordão. Ao amanhecer, não tinha ficado ninguém que não houvesse atravessado o Jordão.
pt.R: Então Davi e todo o seu povo se levantaram e atravessaram o rio Jordão. Quando o sol nasceu, todos já estavam do outro lado.

am.L: ዳዊትና ከእርሱ ጋር የነበረው ሕዝብ ሁሉ ተነሥተው ዮርዳኖስን ተሻገሩ፤ እስከ ንጋትም ብርሃን ድረስ ዮርዳኖስን ሳይሻገር የቀረ አንድ እንኳ አልነበረም።
am.B: ስለዚህ ዳዊትና ከእርሱ ጋር የነበረው ሕዝብ ሁሉ ተነሥተው ዮርዳኖስን ተሻገሩ። ሲነጋም ዮርዳኖስን ሳይሻገር የቀረ አንድም ሰው አልነበረም።
am.R: ስለዚህ ዳዊትና ሕዝቡ ሁሉ ተነሥተው የዮርዳኖስን ወንዝ ተሻገሩ። ፀሐይ ስትወጣም ሁሉም ተሻግረው ነበር።

decisions.choice: not one was missing who had not crossed: all of them crossed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew piles up negatives for emphasis: "until one, not was missing who had not crossed". It means that every last person was over the river before dawn.

decisions.choice: crossed the Jordan: out of immediate reach
decisions.reason: With the river between them and Jerusalem, David's company was safe from a sudden night attack and could move on to Mahanaim (verse 24).

decisions.choice: every one of them was across
decisions.reason: Readable turns the double negative into a plain positive statement.

source.text: וַאֲחִיתֹ֣פֶל רָאָ֗ה כִּ֣י לֹ֣א נֶעֶשְׂתָה֮ עֲצָתוֹ֒ וַיַּחֲבֹ֣שׁ אֶֽת־הַחֲמ֗וֹר וַיָּ֜קָם וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ֙ אֶל־עִיר֔וֹ וַיְצַ֥ו אֶל־בֵּית֖וֹ וַיֵּחָנַ֑ק וַיָּ֕מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּקֶ֥בֶר אָבִֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Ahithophel saw that not was done his counsel, and he saddled the donkey and arose and went to his house, to his city; and he gave orders to his house and strangled himself and died, and was buried in [the] tomb of his father.

en.L: And Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been done, and he saddled the donkey and arose and went to his house, to his city. And he gave orders to his house, and he hanged himself and died, and he was buried in the tomb of his father.
en.B: Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been carried out. He saddled his donkey and set off for home, to his own town. He put his household in order and then hanged himself. So he died, and they buried him in his father's tomb.
en.R: Ahithophel saw that Absalom had not taken his advice. So he saddled his donkey and went back home to his own town. He gave orders about his family and property, and then he hanged himself. He died and was buried in his father's tomb.

es.L: Y Ahitofel vio que no se había hecho su consejo, y ensilló el asno y se levantó y se fue a su casa, a su ciudad. Y dio órdenes a su casa, y se ahorcó y murió, y fue sepultado en el sepulcro de su padre.
es.B: Ahitofel vio que no se había seguido su consejo. Ensilló su asno y se fue a su casa, a su propio pueblo. Puso en orden los asuntos de su casa y luego se ahorcó. Así murió, y lo sepultaron en el sepulcro de su padre.
es.R: Ahitofel vio que Absalón no había seguido su consejo. Entonces ensilló su asno y volvió a su casa, en su pueblo. Dio órdenes sobre su familia y sus bienes, y luego se ahorcó. Murió y lo enterraron en la tumba de su padre.

fr.L: Et Ahitofel vit que son conseil n’avait pas été suivi, et il sella l’âne, et se leva, et s’en alla à sa maison, dans sa ville ; et il donna ses ordres à sa maison, et il s’étrangla et mourut, et il fut enseveli dans le tombeau de son père.
fr.B: Quand Ahitofel vit que son conseil n’avait pas été suivi, il sella son âne et partit chez lui, dans sa ville. Il mit ordre à ses affaires, puis il se pendit. Il mourut ainsi, et on l’ensevelit dans le tombeau de son père.
fr.R: Ahitofel a vu qu’Absalom n’avait pas suivi son conseil. Alors il a sellé son âne et il est rentré chez lui, dans sa ville. Il a donné des ordres pour sa famille et ses biens, puis il s’est pendu. Il est mort et on l’a enterré dans le tombeau de son père.

sw.L: Ahithofeli alipoona kwamba shauri lake halikufuatwa, akamtandika punda wake, akainuka akaenda nyumbani kwake, mjini kwake. Akaitolea nyumba yake maagizo, akajinyonga, akafa, akazikwa katika kaburi la baba yake.
sw.B: Ahithofeli alipoona kwamba ushauri wake haukufuatwa, akamtandika punda wake, akaondoka kwenda nyumbani, katika mji wake mwenyewe. Akaiweka nyumba yake katika utaratibu, kisha akajinyonga. Hivyo akafa, wakamzika katika kaburi la baba yake.
sw.R: Ahithofeli alipoona kwamba Absalomu hakufuata ushauri wake, akamtandika punda wake, akarudi nyumbani katika mji wake. Akatoa maagizo kuhusu jamaa yake na mali yake, kisha akajinyonga. Akafa, akazikwa katika kaburi la baba yake.

vi.L: A-hi-tô-phe thấy mưu kế mình không được làm theo, thì thắng yên lừa, đứng dậy đi về nhà mình, về thành của mình. Ông dặn dò nhà mình, rồi tự thắt cổ mà chết, và được chôn trong mộ của cha mình.
vi.B: A-hi-tô-phe thấy lời khuyên của mình không được thực hiện, liền thắng yên lừa và trở về nhà ở quê mình. Ông sắp đặt việc nhà xong thì thắt cổ tự tử. Ông chết và được chôn trong mộ của cha ông.
vi.R: A-hi-tô-phe thấy Áp-sa-lôm không làm theo lời khuyên của mình. Vậy ông thắng yên lừa và trở về nhà ở quê mình. Ông dặn dò mọi việc về gia đình và của cải, rồi thắt cổ tự tử. Ông chết và được chôn trong mộ của cha ông.

ko.L: 아히도벨은 자기 계책이 실행되지 않은 것을 보고, 나귀에 안장을 얹고 일어나 자기 집, 자기 성읍으로 갔다. 그는 자기 집에 명령을 내린 다음 목을 매어 죽었고, 그의 아버지의 무덤에 묻혔다.
ko.B: 아히도벨은 자기 계책이 받아들여지지 않은 것을 보고, 나귀에 안장을 얹고 길을 떠나 고향 성읍에 있는 자기 집으로 갔다. 그는 집안일을 정리한 뒤에 목을 매었다. 그렇게 그는 죽었고, 사람들은 그를 그의 아버지의 무덤에 묻었다.
ko.R: 아히도벨은 압살롬이 자기 계책을 받아들이지 않은 것을 보았다. 그래서 그는 나귀에 안장을 얹고 고향 성읍에 있는 자기 집으로 돌아갔다. 그는 가족과 재산에 관한 일을 정리한 다음 목을 매었다. 그는 죽어서 그의 아버지의 무덤에 묻혔다.

pt.L: E Aitofel viu que o seu conselho não tinha sido seguido, e selou o jumento, e se levantou, e foi para a sua casa, para a sua cidade. E deu ordens à sua casa, e se enforcou, e morreu, e foi sepultado no sepulcro do seu pai.
pt.B: Quando Aitofel viu que o seu conselho não tinha sido seguido, selou o jumento e partiu para casa, para a sua cidade. Pôs a sua casa em ordem e se enforcou. Assim ele morreu e foi sepultado no túmulo do seu pai.
pt.R: Aitofel viu que Absalão não tinha seguido o seu conselho. Então selou o jumento e voltou para casa, na sua cidade. Deu ordens sobre a família e os bens, e depois se enforcou. Ele morreu e foi sepultado no túmulo do pai.

am.L: አኪጦፌልም ምክሩ እንዳልተደረገ ባየ ጊዜ አህያውን ጫነ፤ ተነሥቶም ወደ ቤቱ ወደ ከተማው ሄደ፤ ለቤቱም አዘዘ፤ ራሱንም ሰቀለ፤ ሞተም፤ በአባቱም መቃብር ተቀበረ።
am.B: አኪጦፌል ምክሩ ተግባራዊ እንዳልሆነ ባየ ጊዜ አህያውን ኮርቻ ጭኖ ወደ ገዛ ከተማው ወደ ቤቱ ሄደ። ቤቱንም አስተካክሎ ራሱን ሰቀለ። እንዲህም ሞተ፤ በአባቱም መቃብር ቀበሩት።
am.R: አኪጦፌል አቤሴሎም ምክሩን እንዳልተቀበለ ባየ ጊዜ አህያውን ኮርቻ ጭኖ ወደ ገዛ ከተማው ወደ ቤቱ ተመለሰ። ስለ ቤተሰቡና ስለ ንብረቱ ትእዛዝ ሰጠ፤ ከዚያም ራሱን ሰቀለ። ሞተም፤ በአባቱም መቃብር ተቀበረ።

decisions.choice: Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been done: he foresaw the end
decisions.reason: The text gives no reason for what he did next beyond this. The story implies that Ahithophel saw that Absalom's cause was now lost, and that as David's adviser who had turned against him he could expect no mercy.

decisions.choice: gave orders to his house: set his affairs in order
decisions.reason: The phrase means giving final instructions to one's household before death (2 Kings 20:1; Isaiah 38:1).

decisions.choice: his city: Giloh
decisions.reason: Ahithophel came from Giloh in the hill country of Judah (15:12).

decisions.choice: hanged himself: the end of the betrayer
decisions.reason: The verb means to strangle oneself. Ahithophel, the trusted friend who turned against David (compare Psalm 41:10; 55:13-15), dies by his own hand. The early Greek translation of this verse uses the same verb that Matthew 27:5 uses of Judas.

decisions.choice: buried in his father's tomb: an ordinary family burial
decisions.reason: Families were buried together in a family tomb. Ahithophel is buried with his father in the normal way; the text passes no further judgment.

decisions.choice: Absalom had not taken
decisions.reason: Readable supplies who did not follow the advice, since the Hebrew uses a passive.

decisions.choice: put his household in order
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom (see m2).

decisions.choice: deu ordens à sua casa (L); Pôs a sua casa em ordem (B); se enforcou
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase; Balanced says "pôs a sua casa em ordem", the Portuguese idiom for final instructions before death (m2). "Enforcar-se" is the verb Matthew 27:5 uses in Portuguese for Judas, so the link the meaning note points to (m4) is kept.

source.text: וְדָוִ֖ד בָּ֣א מַחֲנָ֑יְמָה וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֗ם עָבַר֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן ה֕וּא וְכָל־אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And David had come to Mahanaim, and Absalom had crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.

en.L: And David had come to Mahanaim, and Absalom had crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.
en.B: David had reached Mahanaim by the time Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
en.R: David arrived at the town of Mahanaim. Meanwhile Absalom and all the army of Israel crossed the Jordan River.

es.L: Y David había llegado a Mahanaim, y Absalón había pasado el Jordán, él y todos los hombres de Israel con él.
es.B: David ya había llegado a Mahanaim cuando Absalón cruzó el Jordán con todos los hombres de Israel.
es.R: David llegó al pueblo de Mahanaim. Mientras tanto, Absalón y todo el ejército de Israel cruzaron el río Jordán.

fr.L: Et David était arrivé à Mahanaïm, et Absalom avait passé le Jourdain, lui et tout homme d’Israël avec lui.
fr.B: David avait atteint Mahanaïm lorsque Absalom passa le Jourdain avec tous les hommes d’Israël.
fr.R: David est arrivé à la ville de Mahanaïm. Pendant ce temps, Absalom et toute l’armée d’Israël ont traversé le Jourdain.

sw.L: Daudi alikuwa amefika Mahanaimu, na Absalomu akavuka Yordani, yeye na watu wote wa Israeli pamoja naye.
sw.B: Daudi alikuwa amekwisha kufika Mahanaimu wakati Absalomu alipovuka Yordani pamoja na watu wote wa Israeli.
sw.R: Daudi akafika katika mji wa Mahanaimu. Wakati huo Absalomu na jeshi lote la Israeli wakavuka mto Yordani.

vi.L: Đa-vít đã đến Ma-ha-na-im, còn Áp-sa-lôm đã qua sông Giô-đanh, chàng và mọi người Y-sơ-ra-ên theo chàng.
vi.B: Đa-vít đã đến Ma-ha-na-im khi Áp-sa-lôm cùng mọi người Y-sơ-ra-ên qua sông Giô-đanh.
vi.R: Đa-vít đến thành Ma-ha-na-im. Trong khi đó Áp-sa-lôm và toàn quân Y-sơ-ra-ên qua sông Giô-đanh.

ko.L: 다윗은 마하나임에 이르렀고, 압살롬은 그와 함께한 이스라엘의 모든 사람과 함께 요단강을 건넜다.
ko.B: 압살롬이 이스라엘의 모든 사람을 거느리고 요단강을 건넜을 때, 다윗은 이미 마하나임에 이르러 있었다.
ko.R: 다윗은 마하나임 성에 이르렀다. 그동안 압살롬과 이스라엘의 온 군대는 요단강을 건넜다.

pt.L: E Davi tinha chegado a Maanaim, e Absalão atravessou o Jordão, ele e todos os homens de Israel com ele.
pt.B: Davi já tinha chegado a Maanaim quando Absalão atravessou o Jordão com todos os homens de Israel.
pt.R: Davi chegou à cidade de Maanaim. Enquanto isso, Absalão e todo o exército de Israel atravessaram o rio Jordão.

am.L: ዳዊትም ወደ መሃናይም መጥቶ ነበር፤ አቤሴሎምም እርሱና ከእርሱ ጋር የነበሩት የእስራኤል ሰዎች ሁሉ ዮርዳኖስን ተሻገሩ።
am.B: አቤሴሎም ከእስራኤል ሰዎች ሁሉ ጋር ዮርዳኖስን በተሻገረ ጊዜ ዳዊት መሃናይም ደርሶ ነበር።
am.R: ዳዊት መሃናይም ወደምትባለው ከተማ ደረሰ። በዚህ መካከል አቤሴሎምና የእስራኤል ሠራዊት ሁሉ የዮርዳኖስን ወንዝ ተሻገሩ።

decisions.choice: David had come ... Absalom had crossed: two events side by side
decisions.reason: Both clauses put the subject first, which sets the two movements side by side: David was already in Mahanaim when Absalom crossed after him.

decisions.choice: Mahanaim: a town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Mahanaim lay in Gilead, east of the Jordan. It had been the capital of Saul's son Ishbosheth (2:8-9).

decisions.choice: every man of Israel: the army Absalom raised
decisions.reason: Absalom followed Hushai's advice and gathered all Israel (verse 11). "Every man of Israel" here is the fighting force of the tribes that followed him.

decisions.choice: all the army of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "army" because these are the men gathered to fight (see m3).

decisions.choice: Maanaim
decisions.reason: "Maanaim", the form set in 2:8 for the whole book (m2), without the English "h" Portuguese does not pronounce.

source.text: וְאֶת־עֲמָשָׂ֗א שָׂ֧ם אַבְשָׁלֹ֛ם תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָ֖ב עַל־הַצָּבָ֑א וַעֲמָשָׂ֣א בֶן־אִ֗ישׁ וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יִתְרָ֣א הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־בָּא֙ אֶל־אֲבִיגַ֣ל בַּת־נָחָ֔שׁ אֲח֥וֹת צְרוּיָ֖ה אֵ֥ם יוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And Amasa had set Absalom instead of Joab over the army; and Amasa [was the] son of a man and his name [was] Ithra the Israelite, who had gone into Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, mother of Joab.

en.L: And Absalom had set Amasa over the army in place of Joab. And Amasa [was the] son of a man whose name [was] Ithra the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
en.B: Absalom had put Amasa in command of the army instead of Joab. Amasa's father was a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had slept with Abigail daughter of Nahash, the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
en.R: Absalom had made Amasa commander of his army in place of Joab. Amasa's father was a man named Ithra the Israelite. His mother was Abigail, who was the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother. So Amasa and Joab were cousins.

es.L: Y Absalón había puesto a Amasa sobre el ejército en lugar de Joab. Y Amasa [era] hijo de un hombre cuyo nombre [era] Itra el israelita, que se había llegado a Abigail hija de Nahas, hermana de Sarvia, la madre de Joab.
es.B: Absalón había puesto a Amasa al mando del ejército en lugar de Joab. El padre de Amasa era un hombre llamado Itra el israelita, que se había acostado con Abigail hija de Nahas, hermana de Sarvia, la madre de Joab.
es.R: Absalón había nombrado a Amasa jefe de su ejército en lugar de Joab. El padre de Amasa era un hombre llamado Itra el israelita. Su madre era Abigail, hija de Nahas y hermana de Sarvia, la madre de Joab. Así que Amasa y Joab eran primos.

fr.L: Et Absalom avait établi Amasa sur l’armée à la place de Joab. Et Amasa [était] le fils d’un homme dont le nom [était] Yitra l’Israélite, qui était allé vers Abigaïl, fille de Nahash, sœur de Tserouya, la mère de Joab.
fr.B: Absalom avait mis Amasa à la tête de l’armée à la place de Joab. Le père d’Amasa était un homme nommé Yitra l’Israélite, qui avait couché avec Abigaïl, fille de Nahash et sœur de Tserouya, la mère de Joab.
fr.R: Absalom avait nommé Amasa chef de son armée à la place de Joab. Le père d’Amasa était un homme nommé Yitra l’Israélite. Sa mère était Abigaïl, la fille de Nahash et la sœur de Tserouya, la mère de Joab. Amasa et Joab étaient donc cousins.

sw.L: Absalomu alikuwa amemweka Amasa juu ya jeshi mahali pa Yoabu. Amasa [alikuwa] mwana wa mtu ambaye jina lake [lilikuwa] Yithra Mwisraeli, aliyekuwa ameingia kwa Abigaili binti Nahashi, dada wa Seruya, mama yake Yoabu.
sw.B: Absalomu alikuwa amemweka Amasa kuwa mkuu wa jeshi badala ya Yoabu. Baba yake Amasa alikuwa mtu aitwaye Yithra Mwisraeli, aliyekuwa amelala na Abigaili binti Nahashi, dada wa Seruya, mama yake Yoabu.
sw.R: Absalomu alikuwa amemfanya Amasa kuwa mkuu wa jeshi lake mahali pa Yoabu. Baba yake Amasa alikuwa mtu aitwaye Yithra Mwisraeli. Mama yake alikuwa Abigaili, binti Nahashi na dada wa Seruya, mama yake Yoabu. Kwa hiyo Amasa na Yoabu walikuwa binamu.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm đã lập A-ma-sa chỉ huy quân đội thay cho Giô-áp. A-ma-sa [là] con trai một người tên [là] Gít-ra người Y-sơ-ra-ên, người đã ăn ở với A-bi-ga-in con gái Na-hách, em gái Xê-ru-gia mẹ Giô-áp.
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm đã lập A-ma-sa làm tướng chỉ huy quân đội thay cho Giô-áp. Cha của A-ma-sa là một người tên Gít-ra, người Y-sơ-ra-ên, đã ăn ở với A-bi-ga-in con gái Na-hách, em gái Xê-ru-gia mẹ Giô-áp.
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm đã cho A-ma-sa làm tướng chỉ huy quân đội của mình thay cho Giô-áp. Cha của A-ma-sa là một người tên Gít-ra, người Y-sơ-ra-ên. Mẹ ông là A-bi-ga-in, con gái Na-hách và là em gái của Xê-ru-gia, mẹ Giô-áp. Vậy A-ma-sa và Giô-áp là anh em họ.

ko.L: 압살롬은 요압 대신 아마사를 군대 위에 세웠다. 아마사는 이드라라는 이스라엘 사람의 아들이었는데, 이드라는 요압의 어머니 스루야의 자매인 나하스의 딸 아비갈에게 들어갔던 사람이었다.
ko.B: 압살롬은 요압 대신 아마사를 군대 사령관으로 세웠다. 아마사의 아버지는 이스라엘 사람 이드라였는데, 그는 나하스의 딸 아비갈과 동침했다. 아비갈은 요압의 어머니 스루야의 자매였다.
ko.R: 압살롬은 요압 대신 아마사를 자기 군대의 사령관으로 삼았다. 아마사의 아버지는 이스라엘 사람 이드라였다. 아마사의 어머니는 아비갈이었는데, 나하스의 딸이며 요압의 어머니 스루야의 자매였다. 그러니 아마사와 요압은 사촌이었다.

pt.L: E Absalão tinha posto Amasa sobre o exército em lugar de Joabe. E Amasa [era] filho de um homem cujo nome [era] Itra, o israelita, que tinha se deitado com Abigail, filha de Naás, irmã de Zeruia, mãe de Joabe.
pt.B: Absalão tinha posto Amasa no comando do exército, em lugar de Joabe. O pai de Amasa era um homem chamado Itra, o israelita, que tinha tido relações com Abigail, filha de Naás e irmã de Zeruia, a mãe de Joabe.
pt.R: Absalão tinha feito de Amasa o comandante do seu exército, no lugar de Joabe. O pai de Amasa era um homem chamado Itra, o israelita. A mãe dele era Abigail, filha de Naás e irmã de Zeruia, a mãe de Joabe. Assim, Amasa e Joabe eram primos.

am.L: አቤሴሎምም በኢዮአብ ፋንታ አሜሳይን በሠራዊቱ ላይ ሾሞት ነበር። አሜሳይም ስሙ ይትራ የተባለ የእስራኤላዊ ሰው ልጅ [ነበረ]፤ እርሱም የኢዮአብ እናት የጽሩያ እኅት ወደ ሆነችው ወደ ናዖስ ልጅ ወደ አቢግያ ገብቶ ነበር።
am.B: አቤሴሎም በኢዮአብ ፋንታ አሜሳይን የሠራዊቱ አለቃ አድርጎ ሾሞት ነበር። የአሜሳይ አባት ይትራ የተባለ እስራኤላዊ ሰው ነበረ፤ እርሱም የኢዮአብ እናት የጽሩያ እኅት ከሆነችው ከናዖስ ልጅ ከአቢግያ ጋር ተኝቶ ነበር።
am.R: አቤሴሎም በኢዮአብ ፋንታ አሜሳይን የሠራዊቱ አለቃ አድርጎ ሾሞት ነበር። የአሜሳይ አባት ይትራ የተባለ እስራኤላዊ ሰው ነበረ። እናቱም የናዖስ ልጅ አቢግያ ነበረች፤ እርሷም የኢዮአብ እናት የጽሩያ እኅት ነበረች። ስለዚህ አሜሳይና ኢዮአብ የእኅትማማቾች ልጆች ነበሩ።

decisions.choice: the Israelite
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text here calls Ithra "the Israelite". The list in 1 Chronicles 2:17 calls him "Jether the Ishmaelite", and some manuscripts of the early Greek translation of Samuel read "the Jezreelite". Calling a man in Israel "the Israelite" would be strange unless it set him apart from something else, so the Chronicles reading may be the original; the Hebrew text of Samuel is followed here.

decisions.choice: Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah: David's half-sister
alternatives: daughter of Nahash, as her mother's name
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 2:13-17 lists Zeruiah and Abigail as sisters of David, daughters of Jesse. Here their parent is Nahash. Nahash may have been their mother, or their father before their mother married Jesse; the text does not explain. Either way Amasa and Joab were cousins and both nephews of David.

decisions.choice: had gone in to: had sexual relations with
decisions.reason: "Go in to" a woman is a common way of speaking of sexual union, used both of marriage (Genesis 29:21) and of other relationships. The text does not say whether Ithra and Abigail were married.

decisions.choice: over the army: commander of the army
decisions.reason: Joab, son of Zeruiah, was David's commander of the army (8:16). Absalom replaces him with Joab's own cousin; the two will meet again in 19:14 and 20:8-10.

decisions.choice: So Amasa and Joab were cousins
decisions.reason: Readable states the family link the verse is giving, since the list of names is hard to follow.

decisions.choice: had slept with
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain expression that, like the Hebrew, does not say whether they were married (see m3).

decisions.choice: Yitra, Abigaïl, Nahash
decisions.reason: Yitra transcribes the Hebrew with "y", as the Samuel terms note writes Yabesh; Abigaïl is the form the note gives for Nabal’s wife, used here for this other woman of the same name.

decisions.choice: Amasa; Itra el israelita; Abigail hija de Nahas
decisions.reason: Amasa as the terms note; Itra and Nahas keep the usual Spanish spelling. Abigail here is David's sister, a different woman from Nabal's widow, but the Hebrew names are the same and so is the Spanish.

decisions.choice: Yithra, Abigaili binti Nahashi
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note follow the usual Swahili pattern, ending in a vowel; this Abigail takes the same form as David's wife Abigaili in the terms note, though she is another woman, David's sister.

decisions.choice: "A-ma-sa", "Gít-ra", "A-bi-ga-in", "Na-hách"; Abigail is "em gái" of Zeruiah
decisions.reason: Names as the Samuel terms note and the usual Vietnamese forms; Vietnamese must say older or younger sister, and Zeruiah, mother of David's oldest commanders, is taken as the older.

decisions.choice: "아비갈" for Amasa's mother
decisions.reason: The Hebrew spells this woman's name in a shorter form than that of Nabal's wife (1 Samuel 25), and Korean keeps the short form so that the two women are not confused; the English uses "Abigail" for both.

decisions.choice: Amasa; Itra, o israelita; Abigail, filha de Naás; tinha se deitado com (L), tinha tido relações com (B)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 19:13; 20:4-12): "Amasa" and "Itra", the usual Brazilian forms; "Abigail" and "Naás" keep the spellings of 1 Samuel 25 and 11:1, though these are other people (m2). Literal says "deitar-se com" here and Balanced "ter relações com", which, like the Hebrew, do not say whether they were married (m3).

decisions.choice: Names: "አሜሳይ" (Amasa), "ይትራ" (Ithra), "አቢግያ" (Abigail), "ናዖስ" (Nahash), "ጽሩያ" (Zeruiah).

decisions.choice: Shobi son of Nahash: a son of the Ammonite king
decisions.reason: Nahash had been king of the Ammonites and had shown David kindness (10:1-2). His son Hanun insulted David's envoys, and David later took Rabbah, the Ammonite capital (12:26-31). Shobi, another son of Nahash, now comes to David's aid; he may have been ruling Rabbah under David. This Nahash is probably a different person from the Nahash of verse 25.

decisions.choice: Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar: the man who had sheltered Mephibosheth
decisions.reason: Machir had given a home to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth until David brought him to Jerusalem (9:4-5).

decisions.choice: Barzillai the Gileadite: a rich old man of Gilead
decisions.reason: Barzillai was a very old and wealthy man; David later wished to reward him at court (19:32-40; 1 Kings 2:7).

decisions.choice: three men came to help him
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long Hebrew sentence into shorter ones and supplies a verb so that the first can stand on its own; the gifts follow in verses 28-29.

decisions.reason: Usual French transcriptions ("k" for Makir, "gu" for the hard g, the diaeresis in Barzillaï); kept for both books.

decisions.reason: These names take their usual Spanish spelling and stay the same through the block (Maquir and Lodebar as in chapter 9; Barzilai again in chapter 19).

decisions.choice: Shobi, Raba, Makiri mwana wa Amieli, Lo-debari, Barzilai Mgileadi, Rogelimu
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note, in the usual Swahili pattern; a man of Gilead is "Mgileadi". Used the same way in chapter 19.

decisions.choice: "Sô-bi", "Ráp-ba", "Ma-ki", "A-mi-ên", "Lô-đê-ba", "Bát-xi-lai", "Rô-ghê-lim"
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese forms of these names, kept through Samuel. Like the Hebrew, Literal and Balanced run the sentence on into verse 29.

decisions.choice: one Korean sentence across verses 27-29: the givers (27), the gifts (28-29), and "가져왔다" in verse 29
alternatives: moving "brought" into verse 28, as the English Balanced does
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last, so the Hebrew order (the givers, the list, then "they brought") fits without moving words across a verse boundary. Readable splits the sentence, as the English Readable does.

decisions.reason: "Roasted grain" appears twice in the list. It may have been copied twice by mistake; the early Greek translation does not repeat it. Or the second may name roasted seeds of the beans and lentils just listed. Either way roasted grain was among the gifts.

decisions.choice: bedding: beds or sleeping mats
decisions.reason: The word means a place to lie down. In this list it means bedding or mats for the weary company.

decisions.choice: basins and potter's vessels: bowls and clay pots
decisions.reason: These were the ordinary dishes and pots needed to cook and eat.

decisions.choice: the list is the object of "brought" in verse 29
decisions.reason: The verb comes only in verse 29, after all the goods have been named.

decisions.choice: brought
decisions.reason: Balanced moves the verb "brought" up to the start of the list, as English needs, and leaves out the repeated "roasted grain" (see m1); verse 29 does not repeat the verb.

decisions.choice: They brought ... They also brought
decisions.reason: Readable puts the list in short sentences of its own and lists roasted grain once.

decisions.choice: bisi (roasted grain)
decisions.reason: "Bisi" is the everyday Swahili word for grain roasted on the fire; Literal keeps it twice, as the Hebrew names it twice, and Balanced and Readable once, as the English does.

decisions.choice: camas; grãos tostados (twice at L, once at B and R)
decisions.reason: "Camas" covers beds or sleeping mats (m2). "Grãos tostados" is the roasted grain of Ruth 2:14 in Portuguese; Literal keeps it twice as the Hebrew has it (m1), Balanced and Readable once, as the English does. "Favas" names the beans of the ancient Near East; "feijão" would suggest the American bean.

decisions.choice: "ቆሎ" for the roasted grain (both times at Literal).
decisions.reason: ቆሎ is the ordinary Amharic word for grain roasted to eat, the food the Hebrew names.

decisions.choice: Literal and Balanced keep the list as the object of "አመጡ" (brought) in verse 29; Readable makes verse 28 its own sentences.
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the verb last, which the Hebrew's order across verses 27-29 already allows: the givers in 27, the gifts in 28-29, the verb in 29.

records.literal_gloss: And honey and curds and sheep and cheese of [the] herd, they brought for David and for the people which [was] with him to eat; for they said, the people [is] hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.

en.L: and honey and curds and sheep and cheese of the herd. They brought [these] for David and for the people who [were] with him to eat, for they said, "The people [are] hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."
en.B: honey and curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd, as food for David and the people with him. They said, "The people have become hungry and tired and thirsty in the wilderness."
en.R: And they brought honey, curds, sheep and cheese from cows. All this was for David and his people to eat. The men said to themselves, "These people must be hungry, tired and thirsty out in the wilderness."

es.L: y miel y cuajada y ovejas y quesos de vaca. [Los] trajeron para que comieran David y el pueblo que [estaba] con él, porque dijeron: «El pueblo [está] hambriento y cansado y sediento en el desierto».
es.B: miel y cuajada, ovejas y quesos de vaca, para que comieran David y la gente que estaba con él. Decían: «La gente está hambrienta, cansada y sedienta en el desierto».
es.R: También trajeron miel, cuajada, ovejas y quesos de vaca. Todo esto era para que comieran David y su gente. Los hombres pensaron: «Esta gente debe de estar hambrienta, cansada y con sed allá en el desierto».

fr.L: du miel, du lait caillé, des moutons et des fromages de vache. Ils [les] apportèrent à David et au peuple qui [était] avec lui pour manger, car ils disaient : « Le peuple [est] affamé, fatigué et assoiffé dans le désert. »
fr.B: du miel et du lait caillé, des moutons et des fromages de vache, pour nourrir David et le peuple qui l’accompagnait. Ils se disaient : « Le peuple a faim, il est fatigué et il a soif dans le désert. »
fr.R: Et ils ont apporté du miel, du lait caillé, des moutons et des fromages de vache. Tout cela, c’était pour que David et son peuple puissent manger. Les hommes se disaient : « Ces gens doivent avoir faim, être fatigués et avoir soif dans le désert. »

sw.L: na asali na maziwa mgando na kondoo na jibini ya ng'ombe. Wakamletea Daudi na watu waliokuwa pamoja naye [vitu hivi] ili wale, kwa maana walisema, "Watu [wana] njaa na wamechoka na wana kiu nyikani."
sw.B: asali na maziwa mgando, kondoo, na jibini ya ng'ombe, ili viwe chakula cha Daudi na watu waliokuwa pamoja naye. Walisema, "Watu wamepatwa na njaa, uchovu na kiu huko nyikani."
sw.R: Wakaleta pia asali, maziwa mgando, kondoo na jibini ya maziwa ya ng'ombe. Vyote hivyo vilikuwa chakula cha Daudi na watu wake. Watu hao waliwaza, "Watu hawa lazima wana njaa, wamechoka na wana kiu huko nyikani."

vi.L: mật ong, sữa đông, chiên, và phô mai bò. Họ đem [những thứ này] đến cho Đa-vít và dân theo vua ăn, vì họ nói: "Dân chúng đói, mệt và khát trong hoang mạc."
vi.B: mật ong, sữa đông, chiên và phô mai bò, để Đa-vít và dân theo vua ăn. Họ nói: "Dân chúng đã đói, mệt và khát trong hoang mạc."
vi.R: Họ còn đem đến mật ong, sữa đông, chiên và phô mai làm từ sữa bò. Tất cả là để cho Đa-vít và người của vua ăn. Họ nghĩ: "Những người này hẳn đang đói, mệt và khát ngoài hoang mạc."

ko.L: 꿀과 엉긴 젖과 양과 소젖 치즈를, 다윗과 그와 함께 있는 백성이 먹도록 가져왔다. 그들이 "백성이 광야에서 굶주리고 지치고 목마르다" 하고 말했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 꿀과 엉긴 젖과 양과 소젖으로 만든 치즈를 다윗과 그와 함께 있는 백성에게 먹을 것으로 가져왔다. 그들은 "백성이 광야에서 굶주리고 지치고 목말랐을 것이다" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 그리고 꿀과 엉긴 젖과 양과 소젖으로 만든 치즈도 가져왔다. 이것은 모두 다윗과 그의 백성이 먹으라고 가져온 것이었다. 그들은 "이 사람들이 광야에서 틀림없이 배고프고 지치고 목마를 것이다" 하고 생각했다.

pt.L: e mel, e coalhada, e ovelhas, e queijo de vacas. Trouxeram [isso] para Davi e para o povo que [estava] com ele comerem, porque disseram: "O povo [está] faminto, e cansado, e sedento no deserto."
pt.B: mel e coalhada, ovelhas e queijo de vaca, para Davi e o povo que estava com ele comerem. Pois disseram: "O povo está com fome, cansado e com sede no deserto."
pt.R: Trouxeram ainda mel, coalhada, ovelhas e queijo de vaca. Tudo isso era para Davi e o seu povo comerem. Os homens pensaram: "Essa gente deve estar com fome, cansada e com sede aí no deserto."

am.L: ማርንና እርጎን፣ በጎችንና የከብት አይብን፤ ለዳዊትና ከእርሱ ጋር ለነበረው ሕዝብ እንዲበሉ [እነዚህን] አመጡ፤ «ሕዝቡ በምድረ በዳ ተርቧል፤ ደክሟል፤ ተጠምቷልም» ብለው ነበርና።
am.B: ማርንና እርጎን፣ በጎችንና የከብት አይብን ለዳዊትና ከእርሱ ጋር ለነበረው ሕዝብ ምግብ እንዲሆን አመጡ። «ሕዝቡ በምድረ በዳ ተርቧል፤ ደክሟል፤ ተጠምቷልም» ብለው ነበርና።
am.R: ደግሞም ማር፣ እርጎ፣ በጎችና የላም አይብ አመጡ። ይህ ሁሉ ዳዊትና ሕዝቡ እንዲበሉት ነበር። ሰዎቹ፦ «እነዚህ ሰዎች በምድረ በዳ ተርበው፣ ደክመውና ተጠምተው መሆን አለበት» ብለው በልባቸው አስበው ነበር።

decisions.choice: cheese of the herd: a product of cow's milk
decisions.reason: The first word occurs only here. It seems to name cheese or thickened cream made from the milk of cattle.

decisions.choice: they said: they thought
decisions.reason: "Said" here may mean that they said it to one another or that they thought it. Their words give the reason for their gifts.

decisions.choice: hungry, weary and thirsty in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The words may recall Israel in the wilderness, hungry and thirsty, where God provided for his people (Exodus 16-17). Here the provision comes through men east of the Jordan, one of them an Ammonite.

decisions.choice: curds: thickened milk
decisions.reason: The word names curdled milk or soft butter, a common food (Genesis 18:8; Judges 5:25).

decisions.choice: said to themselves; must be
decisions.reason: Readable takes "said" as what they thought (see m2) and adds "must be" to show it was their judgment.

decisions.choice: They brought [these]
decisions.reason: Literal starts a new sentence at the verb that completes the list of verses 27-28.

decisions.choice: coalhada; queijo de vacas (L), queijo de vaca (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Coalhada", the thickened milk of Genesis 18:8 and Judges 5:25 (m4); the rare word for the cheese is given as the meaning note reads it, "queijo de vaca" (m1).
